Record Q1 2021 — first quarter exceeding $50M in sales (+78%), driven by over 100% North America growth and 25% international growth.
Gross margin compressed to 41.1% (from 46.1%) on wrapped/imported cans, rework, higher freight, repackaging, raw material and processing costs.
Company was not shipping at full capacity — ~80% fill rate — due to the industry-wide aluminum can shortage and the Texas freeze (shut two co-packers and a warehouse 2.5+ weeks).
Celsius secured cans from Asia, Europe and Canada starting production in March; enough cans for the remainder of 2021 and into 2022; ~50% of 2021 supply will be imported/wrapped.
DSD network expanded to 180+ partners covering ~85% of major metro markets; distributor revenues grew 172%; transitions ongoing with Target, CVS, Walmart, Racetrac, 7-Eleven.
Operating cash use of $13.3M driven by a $19.2M inventory build; ex-inventory/prepaids operations would have generated $8M+ of cash.
Fitness channel recovering — ~10% of North America revenue (vs ~25% pre-COVID), grew ~33% in Q1; pent-up demand expected into summer.
Europe grew ~22% (Nordic-led, +50-51% sequentially) despite COVID lockdowns and FAST protein-snack supply constraints; FAST supply expected to resolve mid/back-half Q2.
FAST brand launching in the US on Amazon in Q2 2021 with 2 SKUs as an exclusive launch.
Amended FY2019 10-K filed same morning re: internal-control disclosure for the October 2019 European acquisition — characterized as technical with no impact to reported figures.
Management does not provide formal guidance; declined to give a target DSD penetration percentage.
Macro headwinds — container/Suez disruption, gas/trucking shortages, inflationary raw-material and transportation costs; promotional architecture being optimized to partially mitigate.
North America sell-in vs. sell-through & can supply

Asked how much of the sequential NA acceleration was sell-in catching up to sell-through, whether accounts went under-served due to can-driven production constraints (pent-up demand), and where the company stands on securing enough cans.

NA grew over 100% (101%) but the company shipped at roughly an 80% fill rate due to wrapped-can slow velocity and the Texas freeze; sell-in limited, sell-out very strong per Nielsen/SPINS/Stackline. Secured cans from Asia, Europe and Canada (production started March), enough for the rest of 2021 and into 2022; mix of imported and US cans persists until US capacity improves. Plans the most production ever in Q2/Q3.
Shelf resets, supply constraints & fitness channel recovery
Asked whether supply limitations would force Celsius to delay shelf-space gains until the April 2022 resets, and for a read on the fitness channel as full reopening approaches plus channel strategy.

Bulk of new resets occur in the April/May window; the company is not limited on new-expansion supply and has enough product to fulfill new distribution. Fitness was ~25% of revenue pre-COVID, currently ~10% of NA revenue, grew ~33% in Q1; continued reopening momentum and pent-up demand expected into summer, though still below pre-pandemic levels.
Asked for more color on Europe over the next couple of quarters, including the FAST brand and its production constraints.

Europe grew ~22% (Nordic-led), ~51% sequentially Q4-to-Q1, despite COVID shutdowns in Finland, Norway and Sweden and FAST protein-snack supply constraints. FAST supply issues should resolve by mid/back-half Q2. The FAST brand launches in the US on Amazon in Q2.
Tropical Vibe, FAST SKUs, powder sticks & customer stickiness

Asked when Tropical Vibe would launch, the number of FAST SKUs coming to Amazon, the trajectory of powder sticks given the can shortage, and color on new customer acquisition, reordering and stickiness.

Tropical Vibe ('What's Your Vibe' summer line) is already available with nationwide 7-Eleven authorization. FAST launches with 2 SKUs on Amazon as an exclusive launch, then scales. Powder sticks/counter products are immaterial to top-line revenue but growing, with rising interest from CVS, Publix and Walmart. Customer stickiness 'extremely positive'; up to 192,000 locations.
DSD penetration ceiling, can shortage resolution & international expansion

Asked the maximum DSD penetration achievable and current penetration; whether the can shortage would be alleviated by year-end and why; and the outlook for Middle East expansion through year-end into 2022.

DSD is core (~85% of major metro markets) but declined to give a target penetration percentage. US can capacity additions should begin coming online in back-half 2021 into 2022, with the consumer return to on-premise a swing factor; Celsius is secured on supply. Exploring UK/Germany; has a Middle East distributor and works with others on an import basis, with no firm timeline. CFO added the distributor model limits footprint and currency risk.
Follow-up asking about marketing intentions for the international rollout — whether the company is pursuing new regions more aggressively and what level of investment that implies.

International rollout uses a distributor/import model with collaborative margin support; fairly limited initially and methodical. The company does not plan to invest heavily ahead of revenue, sticking to its positive-ROI-driven model; any investment will be 'generally immaterial.'
